messages:
Priya: Heads up — we're seeing a spike in `schema_rejects` for fncall legacy outputs in eu-west-1. Multiple customers report 500s + billing attribution weirdness. Anyone able to triage? :eyes:
Sanjeev: On it. do you have an example error payload?
Priya: pasted one below:
```json
{"error":"schema_reject","hook":"fncall","expected_shape":"{object}","received":"[\"some\",\"array\"]","route_id":null,"model_variant":"x-small-degen","request_id":"req_01G..."}
```
Lena: route_id null explains the billing misattribution — if middleware doesn't attach route_id we lose the per-route cost breakdown and it falls into the degen bucket in the dashboard. Was this from the new strict-validate canary?
Priya: Yes, started ~2h after the canary switched to strict mode for fncall validation. Canary config: `strict_mode=true, sample_rate=0.01` but we must've missed fncall shape changes from downstream SDK.
Marta: Product: timeline question — are these actual app errors (user-facing) or internal rejects? If user-facing we need a rollback plan.
Evan: Telemetry note: schema_rejects for fncall historically had very low sampling and we haven't been surfacing `route_id` when payload is malformed. Two issues: (1) sampling hides the scope of the spike, (2) missing metadata prevents proper grouping in console.
ops-bot: [ALERT] 7081234567 - schema_rejects(fncall) spike > 5x baseline in eu-west-1. Ticket created: I-7081234567.
Sanjeev: Quick fix checklist: 1) add fallback to attach `route_id` from parent request before validation; 2) increase sampling for fncall rejects to 10% for next 6h; 3) mute strict canary or revert to permissive soft-validate for fncall. Thoughts?
Lena: Agree. Can we do a config toggle so strict-validate only applies to new tool bindings, not legacy fncall shapes? That would reduce noise.
Marta: We should avoid full rollback unless user impact is confirmed. Priya, any evidence users got 5xx?
Priya: Two customers reported app errors (support thread links) — both use the older SDK that emits arrays for that hook. So it's a compatibility regression.
Evan: I'll patch the telemetry pipeline: ensure `route_id` and `account_id` are captured on reject events (non-null), and add a short-term alert that compares per-route billing delta vs last 24h (threshold 20%). That'll surface misattribution earlier.
Sanjeev: I'll push a hotfix to middleware now (attach route_id from request context if validation removed it). Patch PR: `github.com/redwood/inference/middleware#fix/fncall-routeid`
Priya: After middleware fix, can we flip strict -> soft for fncall in canary and add a post-validate sampler that records full payload for 1% of rejects so we can debug shapes?
Lena: Yes — soft-validate will accept but annotate `validation_status=soft_reject` which still counts for QA without causing 5xx.
Marta: Action items: Evan -> telemetry patch + alert (ETA 1h). Sanjeev -> middleware hotfix + deploy to canary (ETA 30m). Priya -> coordinate with support to identify affected SDK versions. I'll draft a short console banner explaining possible billing misattribution while we fix.
Evan: Also enabling console query for SREs: `SELECT route_id, count(*) FROM schema_rejects WHERE hook='fncall' AND ts > now()-2h GROUP BY route_id;` helps spot null buckets.
Sanjeev: Deployed middleware patch to canary; routing id now preserved on rejects. Monitoring.
ops-bot: [INFO] 7081234567 - middleware canary deploy succeeded.
Priya: Confirmed a drop in degen-bucket counts after the patch. Still seeing samples in soft_reject group — good for debugging.
Marta: OK, keep soft-validate for 48h + increased sampling, then reassess. If telemetry shows no further regressions we'll re-enable strict mode on a smaller slice.
Lena: For long-term: need a compatibility policy for fncall schema evolution + a console UX entry that maps validation rejections to suggested SDK versions or migration notes.
Evan: Filing follow-up: T-7081234567 with telemetry tasks and a dashboard card for schema_rejects by SDK version.
Priya: Thanks all — closing the immediate incident, follow-ups in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
